detailed_description:
[Shot 1] 0.00–8.00seconds, a single medium-wide front three-quarter live-action view of Dante in the frozen chamber. Show head, both hands, torso, upper legs and the entire working weapon envelope with generous side margins. Use a short gentle opening dolly backward to frame the routine, then hold a stable readable viewpoint. No cut, orbit, whip, flash, slow motion or zoom toward the hands. Real weighted leather and solid ice-metal rods, natural short motion blur. Dante's focused confident expression and planted staggered stance support the hand work. The weapon swings at ordinary practiced nunchaku speed, with visible direction changes rather than a rigid helicopter wheel. Only Dante and his one Cerberus are present.

0.00–2.00seconds: Follow the opening handling pattern of <Video 1>. RIGHT glove grips one Cerberus baton; the two free batons remain on their original chains. A right wrist-and-forearm impulse sends the free pair down and out beside the right hip, then up in a compact curving path beside the right shoulder. The arc stays outside the torso. Dante bends the right elbow to receive the returning weapon, reducing its speed rather than snapping the path through his body. LEFT glove reaches beneath the right upper arm and visibly closes around ONE returning free baton. Its fingers grasp the actual baton already attached to the ring, not an invented new rod. The third baton remains visible hanging/swinging in the open air OUTSIDE the right elbow and hip. Show the returning baton approach, the palm receiving it, fingers closing and its speed being arrested. No body penetration.

2.00–4.10seconds: RIGHT glove releases its old baton only after LEFT glove has captured the returning baton. LEFT hand is now the driver, with the previously held right baton and the original third baton both free on their own chains. The left forearm draws a downward/outward curve and sends those free rods around the outside of the left hip, then returns them beside the left shoulder. RIGHT glove reaches below the raised left upper arm to capture ONE returning baton. The spare third branch stays outside the torso, visible under gravity and inertia. The sequence follows the genuine alternating underarm transfer rhythm of <Video 1>, with each catch damping the return and each release preceding the next arc. Contact, release and ownership changes must be visible; no hidden teleport behind the back.

4.10–6.10seconds: As in the middle and later cycles of <Video 1>, RIGHT hand takes over after the catch, left fingers open, and the right wrist drives a compact diagonal figure-eight into a shoulder-height return. Show two rounded changes of direction in open space in front of and beside the body, with consistent depth and occlusion. The solid rods remain on the camera side when crossing the projected torso; they never enter skin, coat, neck or an arm. The body leans and knees flex to create clearance. RIGHT elbow bends to absorb the returning weapon, LEFT glove visibly captures a baton beneath the right arm, then right fingers release. The third rod stays attached, separate and accounted for. Do not immobilize the weapon in a three-baton bundle.

6.10–8.00seconds: LEFT wrist immediately releases the newly free pair into another short outward/downward swing, then brings the weapon back toward a controlled opposite-hand capture. Keep the practiced handling flow of <Video 1> through the final second: drive, arc, return, capture and renewed release. No repeated static pose, long hanging pause, overhead-only wheel, whole-body spin or leap. Show hands actively gripping and opening, chains drawing taut then slackening near a catch, rigid rod lengths and delayed coat motion. End during the next actual swing with both free rods still moving and all three branches continuously attached.
